key_insight: Publicly available policies at U.S. osteopathic medical schools rarely gave clear, scenario-specific support for patient-information decisions, even when related guidance could be found.
clinical_relevance: For institutions and clinicians, the main takeaway is that policy availability does not necessarily translate into actionable guidance for real-world patient-information scenarios.
method: Exploratory vignette-based document analysis of 20 U.S. osteopathic medical schools
Eight patient-information vignettes produced 160 school-vignette evaluations
Each evaluation was run three times with AI-assisted retrieval and rating, then reviewed for discordant cases
evidence_signal: At least one eligible source was found for 159 of 160 pairs, but only 21 pairs (13.1%) were judged to have sufficient support after classification.
watch_item: This was a nonprobability sample of schools and an AI-assisted document review, so results may not generalize broadly and depend on how policies are written and interpreted.
paper_title: Decision Support in Publicly Available Patient Information Policies at U.S. Osteopathic Medical Schools: A Vignette-Based Document Analysis
